#ZeroDay #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
Your browser has a zero-day, and an exploit is already out there. 🌐

What's reported:
→ CVE-2026-125350 is a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component
→ Google says it is aware that an exploit for it exists in the wild
→ An anonymous researcher reported it on 6 Nov; Google shipped the fix on 9 Nov
→ Fixed in Chrome 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac, 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. The same update fixes nine security bugs in total
→ Google hasn't said who is exploiting it or who is targeted

Patch now: Settings → About Chrome, let it update, then click Relaunch. The rollout takes days or weeks, so don't wait for it. On Edge, Brave or Opera, watch for your browser's own fix. Admins: check your fleet's Chrome version, not just the policy.

cover.hook: France says Iran's Revolutionary Guard heated its supermarket freezers.
cover.sub: Around 700 grocery stores. At least 15 fires. France has now named who it blames.

slides.title: Who France blames
slides.body: French authorities accused Iran's IRGC on Monday. A report from France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre names Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC cyber unit that US agencies have linked to CyberAv3ngers.

slides.label: French grocery stores whose refrigeration was sabotaged last month, per the French report
slides.note: At least 15 fires, The Record reports

slides.title: How it worked
slides.body: Per TechCrunch, the hackers broke into web-based controllers that manage fleets of industrial cold units, then raised temperatures to spoil food. Researchers said some affected Danfoss models no longer get security fixes.

slides.title: Not just food
slides.body: A second wave in early November hit businesses in at least 11 European countries, including three sites of France's national blood service. The French Blood Establishment says it was stopped before any blood was spoiled.

slides.title: France's response
slides.body: Iran's ambassador was summoned and France says it will pursue European sanctions. Paris prosecutors opened a case against the unit's head and two deputies and requested international arrest warrants.

slides.title: For anyone running controllers
items: Take refrigeration and building controllers off the public internet
Put remote access behind VPN and MFA, never a bare web login
Replace controllers that no longer get security fixes
Alert on setpoint and defrost changes

items.question: Who in your company owns the fridge, HVAC and building controllers?
items.x_text:
France blames Iran's IRGC for sabotaging refrigeration at ~700 grocery stores. Its report names Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC cyber unit; The Record says at least 15 fires. Hackers got into web-based cold-unit controllers. Get them off the internet.

#OTSecurity #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
Hackers turned supermarket freezers into heaters. France now says it knows who. 🧊🔥

What's reported (The Record, TechCrunch, 9 Nov):
→ French authorities accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of sabotaging refrigeration at around 700 French grocery stores last month
→ The report, from France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre, names Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC cyber unit US agencies have linked to CyberAv3ngers
→ France says the attacks caused extensive food losses and at least 15 fires
→ The hackers broke into web-based controllers that manage fleets of industrial cold units; some affected Danfoss models no longer get security fixes, researchers said
→ A second wave in early November hit at least 11 European countries, including three French blood service sites, stopped before any blood spoiled
→ France summoned Iran's ambassador and says it will pursue EU sanctions

The defender's lesson: building and refrigeration controllers are OT. Keep them off the public internet, put remote access behind VPN and MFA, replace unsupported models and alert on setpoint changes.

items.x_text:
BOSSAI: Acronis says one hacker ran 12 AI agents against hundreds of orgs in 11+ countries, pulling Taipei's 119 fire/ambulance dispatch records for seven districts via an API. The agents failed wherever logins were enforced.

#AISecurity #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
One person. Twelve AI agents. Emergency dispatch records for seven Taipei districts. 🤖

What The Hacker News reported (9 Nov), from Acronis research:
→ A setup called BOSSAI had 12 AI agents, 9 in use, aimed at hundreds of organisations in at least 11 countries
→ It pulled case records from Taipei's 119 fire and ambulance system, covering seven districts, through the system's API. Data was taken or systems accessed at about 10 organisations in Taiwan, Mexico and Thailand
→ Grok and MiniMax refused direct attack requests; the attacker routed other tools through abliterated DeepSeek, GLM and Qwen models
→ The agents made things up too: one scanner invented CVEs
→ Acronis says it is highly confident the attacker is one person in Hualien City, Taiwan

The defender's lesson: the agents failed where logins were enforced, sessions were required and endpoints were filtered. They won on default credentials, open APIs and unpatched databases. AI makes it cheap to try every one of those at once.

cover.hook: 7.7 million shoppers' data may be exposed. Through a cloud service the store used.
cover.sub: Japan's Iris Plaza, run by Iris Ohyama, is still offline while it investigates.

slides.title: What happened
slides.body: Iris Ohyama found the intrusion on 28 Oct. Hackers compromised an external cloud service used by its Iris Plaza shopping platform. It suspended the site, disconnected related systems and says it has blocked the attackers' access.

slides.label: people potentially affected: 5.8 million current and former members plus 1.9 million non-members

slides.title: What data
slides.body: Members: names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, gender and encrypted passwords. Non-members, including guest buyers: names, addresses, phone numbers and emails. The company says the cloud service held no card data.

slides.title: Still offline
slides.body: Iris Plaza, Simple Style and some Iris Group services remain suspended. The company says it has no evidence those other sites were hit, and no reports of unauthorized use or financial damage so far.

slides.title: What to do
items: Expect phishing that uses your real name and address
Change the Iris Plaza password and anywhere you reused it
List every third-party cloud service holding customer data
Review those services' access logs and keys

items.question: Which of your vendors' cloud services hold your customer list?
items.x_text:
Iris Plaza / Iris Ohyama: hackers compromised an external cloud service used by the Japanese shopping platform. 7.7 million people potentially affected: names, addresses, phones, emails; members also DOB and encrypted passwords.

#DataBreach #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
7.7 million people. One cloud service the store relied on. 🛒

What SecurityWeek reported (9 Nov), from Iris Ohyama's statement:
→ Iris Ohyama found the intrusion into its Iris Plaza shopping platform on 28 Oct
→ Hackers compromised an external cloud service the platform used; the company says it has blocked their access and told law enforcement
→ 5.8 million current and former members: names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, gender, encrypted passwords
→ 1.9 million non-members, including guest buyers: names, addresses, phone numbers, emails
→ No card data was stored in that service, and no misuse has been reported so far. Iris Plaza is still offline

The defender's lesson: your customer list lives wherever your vendors put it. Keep an inventory of third-party cloud services holding customer data, and check their access logs and keys. Customers: expect phishing that uses your real details.

items.x_text:
OpenClaw: Acronis counted 575+ malicious agent skills posing as utilities, delivering trojans, crypto miners and infostealers to Windows and macOS. Skills can bundle code that runs with the agent's permissions. Vet them like software.

#AISecurity #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
A skill for your AI agent looks like a few lines of instructions. 575 of them carried malware. 🧩

What Help Net Security reported (10 Nov), from the Acronis TRU Cyber Pulse 2026 report:
→ More than 575 malicious OpenClaw skills posed as utilities
→ They delivered trojans, cryptocurrency miners and information stealers to Windows and macOS
→ Skills can combine instructions with executable code that uses permissions the agent already has
→ Researchers also documented malicious payloads disguised as models, datasets and AI apps on Hugging Face

Myth: a skill is just text. Reality: it's software that runs with your agent's access. Install skills only from sources you trust, read what they execute, keep agents on least privilege and keep approval prompts on.
